# file opened: specials.asm
   1+ C000              ;==============================================================================
   2+ C000              ; Z-POLICE - special monsters (8K page PAGE_SPECIAL, game logic: runs at
   3+ C000              ; $C000 in slot 6)
   4+ C000              ;
   5+ C000              ; Special monsters use the zombie records after the zombies' own (NZOMB ..
   6+ C000              ; NMON-1, zombie.asm), so they share the zombies' drawing (zombie_cell,
   7+ C000              ; fig_draw), map blips, cell marks (zflags), weapon hits and zdamage.  The
   8+ C000              ; record's type (+15) says which monster it is.  Each wave's specials come
   9+ C000              ; from the level file (level_cur, LV_WAVE_DATA: up to LV_SPEC_SLOTS types,
  10+ C000              ; SPEC_*, and how many of each), placed by spec_wave as the wave starts;
  11+ C000              ; the level's start is wave 1 (spec_init).  spec_update moves them each
  12+ C000              ; frame, after zombie_update.
  13+ C000              ;
  14+ C000              ; The ghost (ZT_GHOST, special monster id SPEC_GHOST): a stick man under a white
  15+ C000              ; sheet.  It can't attack the base.  It flies at twice the zombies' speed,
  16+ C000              ; at any angle, and up and down between the ground and the VTOL's ceiling
  17+ C000              ; (MAX_Y), over buildings lower than it.
  18+ C000              ;   * Roaming: it flies in a random direction (a random climb or descent
  19+ C000              ;     too) until something makes it turn: a building in the way or the map
  20+ C000              ;     edge (a new random direction at once), or, at its decision check
  21+ C000              ;     every GHOST_DECIDE (30) frames, a human or the VTOL within GHOST_SEE
  22+ C000              ;     (3 tiles) that it can see.
  23+ C000              ;   * Chasing: it flies straight at the nearest one it can see, aiming
  24+ C000              ;     again every GHOST_TRACK (5) frames.  If it loses sight of its target
  25+ C000              ;     (behind a taller building) or the target is gone, it roams again in a
  26+ C000              ;     random direction, back on the 30-frame cycle.
  27+ C000              ;   * Attacking: within ATTACK_R (0.1 tile) of its target on each axis it
  28+ C000              ;     stops and takes GHOST_DMG hit point every GHOST_HIT_FRAMES (10)
  29+ C000              ;     frames: from a human (HUMAN_HP) until it dies, or from the VTOL
  30+ C000              ;     (vtol_hp, VTOL_HP; at 0 it is destroyed and the game ends).  Its map blip is red
  31+ C000              ;     meanwhile (zatk_flags, zblip_red), as an attacking zombie's.  If the
  32+ C000              ;     target moves out of reach it chases it again; once the human is dead
  33+ C000              ;     it roams again.
  34+ C000              ;   * It has GHOST_HP (10) hit points; any weapon can shoot it.  Killed, it
  35+ C000              ;     fades out where it is, white to near black in 4 steps of 3 frames
  36+ C000              ;     (GM_DYING; zdamage starts it, zombie_draw colours it, g_dying ends
  37+ C000              ;     it), and can't be hit meanwhile.
  38+ C000              ; Ghost record fields, besides the zombies' (zombie.asm):
  39+ C000              ;   +11 frames to its next decision check, +16 mode (GM_*), +17 frames to
  40+ C000              ;   its next blow, +18 hit points, +21,+22 height of its feet, +23,+24 and
  41+ C000              ;   +25,+26 velocity x, z (signed 8.8 units a frame), +27,+28 the x and z
  42+ C000              ;   position fractions, +29 climb (signed units a frame), +30 target
  43+ C000              ;   (TG_NONE, TG_VTOL, or a human's index).
  44+ C000              ;==============================================================================
  45+ C000
  46+ C000              GHOST_HP        equ 10              ; hit points
  47+ C000              GHOST_DECIDE    equ 30              ; frames between decisions while roaming
  48+ C000              GHOST_TRACK     equ 5               ; and while chasing
  49+ C000              GHOST_SEE       equ 3*TILE_UNITS    ; it spots humans / the VTOL this near
  50+ C000              GHOST_HIT_FRAMES equ 10             ; frames between blows
  51+ C000              GHOST_DMG       equ 1               ; hit points a blow
  52+ C000              GHOST_CLIMB     equ 1               ; units a frame up or down
  53+ C000              GHOST_AIM_MIN   equ 80              ; (aiming: nearer counts as this far)
  54+ C000              GM_ROAM         equ 0               ; modes (+16)
  55+ C000              GM_CHASE        equ 1
  56+ C000              GM_ATTACK       equ 2
  57+ C000              GM_DYING        equ 3               ; killed: fading out (+17 frames left)
  58+ C000              GHOST_FADE_FRAMES equ 12            ; the fade: 4 steps of 3 frames
  59+ C000              TG_NONE         equ $FF             ; targets (+30)
  60+ C000              TG_VTOL         equ $FE
  61+ C000              TG_BASE         equ $C0             ; + a base tile's index (base_hp, 0..24)
  62+ C000              ; The banshee (ZT_BANSHEE, id SPEC_BANSHEE): a ghost that flies twice as
  63+ C000              ; fast, reaches BANSHEE_R (0.5 tile), does BANSHEE_DMG a blow and also
  64+ C000              ; attacks the base (the terrace and pad tiles).
  65+ C000              ; The ghoul (ZT_GHOUL, id SPEC_GHOUL, zombie.asm): a half-height zombie
  66+ C000              ; walking at five times the zombies' speed.  It is placed here (spec_wave)
  67+ C000              ; but moved, drawn and hit as a zombie.
  68+ C000              ; The lich (ZT_LICH, id SPEC_LICH): a city's boss, in the last wave of its
  69+ C000              ; last level (the level files).  Placed here (lich_init); walks as a zombie
  70+ C000              ; at 4 times the speed, drawn at LICH_H; shoots fireballs at the VTOL
  71+ C000              ; (lich_update, weapons.asm).  Each city's is harder: LICH_HP + LICH_HP_STEP
  72+ C000              ; hit points a city before it, and a shot every LICH_RATE frames,
  73+ C000              ; LICH_RATE_STEP fewer a city before it, at least LICH_RATE_MIN.  Its
  74+ C000              ; record: +18 and +23 (LICH_HP_HI) its hit points, 16 bits; +24 (LICH_WAIT)
  75+ C000              ; frames to its next shot; +25 (LICH_FRAMES) frames between.
  76+ C000              ; (Which waves have which is the level files' business: gentables.py.)
  77+ C000              BANSHEE_HP      equ 8
  78+ C000              BANSHEE_DMG     equ 5
  79+ C000              BANSHEE_R       equ TILE_UNITS/2
  80+ C000              BASE_TILES      equ (2*TERRACE_R+1)*(2*TERRACE_R+1)
  81+ C000              LICH_HP         equ 50              ; the first city's
  82+ C000              LICH_HP_STEP    equ 25              ; more a city
  83+ C000              LICH_RATE       equ 60              ; the first city's frames between shots
  84+ C000              LICH_RATE_STEP  equ 10              ; fewer a city
  85+ C000              LICH_RATE_MIN   equ 10
  86+ C000
  87+ C000              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  88+ C000              ; A level's start: every special record inactive, then wave 1's specials
  89+ C000              ; (the level's start is wave 1, as any other: spec_wave)
  90+ C000              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  91+ C000              spec_init:

  93+ C004 06 08                ld b,NSPEC

 219+ C10E              ; A new wave began (zwave_new, zombie.asm; spec_init for wave 1): its
 220+ C10E              ; specials from the level file (level_cur, LV_WAVE_DATA: wave_number's
 221+ C10E              ; record), each of its LV_SPEC_SLOTS types (SPEC_NONE: none) as many as it
 222+ C10E              ; says, into free special records.  Waves past LV_MAX_WAVES have none.
 223+ C10E              spec_wave:

   1+ 2000              ;==============================================================================
   2+ 2000              ; Z-POLICE - zombie page (8K page PAGE_ZOMBIE, mapped at $2000 in MMU slot 1)
   3+ 2000              ;
   4+ 2000              ; Placeholder zombies: Layer 2 stick-man silhouettes walking the streets.
   5+ 2000              ; The page stays mapped at $2000 the whole time (slot 0 is used for paging
   6+ 2000              ; Layer 2 sections, slot 7 for the other code pages), so the city page can
   7+ 2000              ; call in here while it draws.
   8+ 2000              ;
   9+ 2000              ; Each zombie is a ZREC-byte record:
  10+ 2000              ;   +0,+1  x  8.8 fixed point in cell units (high byte = cell, low = fraction;
  11+ 2000              ;             the same as world units, one cell = 256)
  12+ 2000              ;   +2,+3  z  likewise
  13+ 2000              ;   +4     heading 0 = +z, 1 = +x, 2 = -z, 3 = -x  (yaw angle = heading*64;
  14+ 2000              ;             heading+1 turns right, heading+3 turns left)
  15+ 2000              ;   +5     walk animation phase 0..3
  16+ 2000              ;   +6     step accumulator: fraction of a world unit (4 bits)
  17+ 2000              ;   +7     wait: frames left standing still (0 = walking)
  18+ 2000              ;   +8,+9  cell (x, z) of the last turn decision ($FF = none)
  19+ 2000              ;   +10    active: 1 = in play, 0 = gone (not moved, linked or drawn)
  20+ 2000              ;   +11    frames until this zombie's next decision check
  21+ 2000              ;   +12,+13  cell (x, z) of its blip on the street map
  22+ 2000              ;   +14    1 = blip plotted
  23+ 2000              ;   +15    type: 0 = zombie, 1 = fast zombie (walks at twice the speed),
  24+ 2000              ;          ZT_GHOUL (a special: 5x, half height), ZT_LICH (a special: 4x,
  25+ 2000              ;          twice the height), ZT_GHOST, ZT_BANSHEE
  26+ 2000              ;   +16    mode: 0 = walking, 1 = going for a base tile, 2 = attacking it
  27+ 2000              ;   +17    frames to its next hit on the tile
  28+ 2000              ;   +18    hit points left (ZHP, ZHP_FAST; weapons.asm zdamage)
  29+ 2000              ;   +19,+20  cell (x, z) marked with CELL_ZOMBIE in city_map ($FF = none)
  30+ 2000              ;   +21,+22  height of its feet (0 for zombies; special monsters fly)
  31+ 2000              ;   +23..+30 special monsters' own fields (specials.asm)
  32+ 2000              ;   +31    1 = drawn last frame (fig_seen; cleared by lock_update, weapons.asm)
  33+ 2000              ;   +32,+33  where: the centre column and row on the view (the missile lock)
  34+ 2000              ; Records 0..NZOMB-1 are the zombies, NZOMB..NMON-1 the special monsters
  35+ 2000              ; (specials.asm), which share the drawing, cell marks, map blips and weapon
  36+ 2000              ; hits; their type (+15) says which.
  37+ 2000              ; zatk_flags (one byte per zombie, by index): TRUE while it attacks a base
  38+ 2000              ; tile, when its map dot is red; FALSE again once the tile is destroyed.
  39+ 2000              ;
  40+ 2000              ; The base: at junctions a zombie leans towards the road that points at the
  41+ 2000              ; landing pad (zbias_t, from the level).  A base tile (terrace or pad) in its
  42+ 2000              ; way isn't avoided: it walks up to ATTACK_R from it and hits it every
  43+ 2000              ; ZHIT_FRAMES frames.  A destroyed terrace tile becomes road and the zombie
  44+ 2000              ; walks on; the pad destroyed sets game_over.
  45+ 2000              ;
  46+ 2000              ; Street map blips: zblip / zblip_off (map.asm) are called on the zombie's
  47+ 2000              ; decision-check frames.  Call zblip_off for a zombie before making it gone.
  48+ 2000              ;
  49+ 2000              ; Decisions are staggered: each active zombie only checks for junctions and
  50+ 2000              ; obstacles once every zsteps frames, with the zombies' check frames spread
  51+ 2000              ; out so only about NZOMB/zsteps of them check on any one frame.  In between
  52+ 2000              ; they just walk, so the look-ahead (zlook) covers zsteps frames of walking
  53+ 2000              ; plus a margin: ZMARGIN + zsteps*zspeed/16.
  54+ 2000              ;
  55+ 2000              ; Movement (zmove), every frame:
  56+ 2000              ;   * Standing still: count the wait down and do nothing else.
  57+ 2000              ;   * Not this zombie's check frame: step forwards (see the last point).
  58+ 2000              ;   * Junctions: once per cell, when the zombie is 0.25-0.75 of the way
  59+ 2000              ;     through the cell along its heading, look for a road (street cell) to
  60+ 2000              ;     the left and to the right.  Left is tested first: if there is a road,
  61+ 2000              ;     turn left at random (1 in 2); if not taken, the same for the right.
  62+ 2000              ;     The cell is then marked as decided, so it isn't tested again until the
  63+ 2000              ;     zombie has been somewhere else.
  64+ 2000              ;   * Blocked (building or map edge within zlook ahead): turn left if there
  65+ 2000              ;     is a road there, else right; otherwise turn round and stand still for
  66+ 2000              ;     ZWAIT frames before testing anything again.
  67+ 2000              ;   * Otherwise step forwards zspeed/16 world units (the remainder is kept,
  68+ 2000              ;     so slow speeds still move smoothly on average).
  69+ 2000              ;
  70+ 2000              ; Zombies are only ever on street (empty) cells.  They are drawn by the city
  71+ 2000              ; traversal when it reaches their cell (draw_cell jumps to zombie_cell for
  72+ 2000              ; empty cells), so the painter's algorithm hides them behind nearer buildings.
  73+ 2000              ; A cell holding zombies has bit 7 (CELL_ZOMBIE) of its city_map byte set,
  74+ 2000              ; by zflags every frame; zombie_cell then searches the records for them.
  75+ 2000              ;
  76+ 2000              ; Sprites (tables_zombie.inc, generated): 8 scales from 1x4 to 8x16 pixels,
  77+ 2000              ; forward and left facings, 4 walk frames.  Rear and right are the mirrored
  78+ 2000              ; forward and left.  One byte per row, bit 7 = leftmost pixel.
  79+ 2000              ;==============================================================================
  80+ 2000
  81+ 2000              NZOMB           equ 40          ; zombie records: the most in a wave
  82+ 2000              NSPEC           equ 8           ; most special monsters (5 ghosts, banshees)
  83+ 2000              NMON            equ NZOMB+NSPEC ; records: zombies, then special monsters
  84+ 2000              ZREC            equ 34          ; bytes per record
  85+ 2000              ZT_FAST         equ 1           ; +15: fast zombie
  86+ 2000              ZT_GHOUL        equ 2           ; +15: a ghoul: a special monster that walks
  87+ 2000                                              ; as a zombie (zmove), half height, 5x speed
  88+ 2000              ZT_LICH         equ 3           ; +15: a lich, a city's boss: a special
  89+ 2000                                              ; monster that walks as a zombie (zmove),
  90+ 2000                                              ; twice the height, 4x speed; it shoots
  91+ 2000                                              ; fireballs (lich_update, weapons.asm)
  92+ 2000              ZT_GHOST        equ 4           ; +15: a ghost (specials.asm); types from
  93+ 2000              ZT_BANSHEE      equ 5           ; here on fly (specials.asm moves them)
  94+ 2000              ZHP             equ 5           ; hit points: a zombie (level 1)
  95+ 2000              ZHP_FAST        equ 4           ; and a fast zombie
  96+ 2000              GHOUL_HP        equ ZHP         ; and a ghoul
  97+ 2000              ZSPEED_INIT     equ 10          ; starting zspeed: 0.63 units (4.9 cm) per
  98+ 2000                                              ; frame, ~0.7 m/s at 14 fps
  99+ 2000              ZSTEPS_INIT     equ 10          ; starting zsteps: decide every 10 frames
 100+ 2000              ZMARGIN         equ 16          ; keep at least this far from walls: 1.25 m
 101+ 2000              ZC_TRIES        equ 16          ; zcluster: places to try near the parent
 102+ 2000              ZC_R            equ 2*TILE_UNITS ;  within 2 tiles of it on x and z
 103+ 2000                      ASSERT 383+128 <= ZC_R          ; (zc_axis)
 104+ 2000              ZWAIT           equ 100         ; frames to stand still when stuck
 105+ 2000              ZOMBIE_H        equ 26          ; height: 2 m (the same as the hit box, ZHIT_H)
 106+ 2000              GHOUL_H         equ ZOMBIE_H/2  ; a ghoul's height: 1 m
 107+ 2000              LICH_H          equ 2*ZOMBIE_H  ; a lich's height: 4 m
 108+ 2000                      ASSERT LICH_H == FIG_LICH_H     ; (gfx_ids.inc)
 109+ 2000                      ASSERT ZSPEED_INIT*5+15 < 256   ; a ghoul's step (zcalc_step) fits
 110+ 2000

 113+ 2000              ; Seed NZOMB zombies at random street positions, away from building walls

 115+ 2000              zombie_init:

 120+ 2008 87                   add a,a                         ; min(ZBIAS_MAX, ZBIAS_BASE +

 124+ 200F 3E 5F                ld a,ZBIAS_MAX

 128+ 2016 06 04                ld b,4

 142+ 2037              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 143+ 2037              ; A wave: the level's LV_ZOMBIES zombies (level_cur; at most NZOMB), LV_FAST
 144+ 2037              ; of them fast, at random street positions; the other zombie records stay
 145+ 2037              ; inactive.  zombie_update calls it again when a wave is wiped out.  (The
 146+ 2037              ; records' cell marks, +19 / +20, are left to zflags: a zombie killed this
 147+ 2037              ; frame may still have one.)  A wave with clusters (a SPEC_CLUSTER entry in
 148+ 2037              ; its level data, the count its clusters): the first few zombies, the
 149+ 2037              ; parents, are placed at random, and the others in turn near each (zcluster).

 290+ 213E              ; HL = the parent's x or z, A = a random byte -> HL = up to ZC_R from it, kept

   1+ 3066              ;==============================================================================
   2+ 3066              ; Z-POLICE - humans to rescue (in the zombie page, after zombie.asm: kept
   3+ 3066              ; mapped in slot 1)
   4+ 3066              ;
   5+ 3066              ; Up to HUMAN_MAX humans, nhumans of them placed at random at start-up (on a
   6+ 3066              ; road, or on a roof low enough to land on).  They stand facing the player,
   7+ 3066              ; and wave their right arm while the VTOL is within WAVE_R.  On the city map
   8+ 3066              ; each is a blue dot, flashing 3 frames on, 3 off.
   9+ 3066              ;
  10+ 3066              ; Fleeing (hum_flee): a human on the road (never one on a roof) with a
  11+ 3066              ; monster within FLEE_R runs from the nearest one for FLEE_TIME frames, at
  12+ 3066              ; HUMAN_FLEE units a frame, then looks again.  Its way is picked at random
  13+ 3066              ; of the two that take it away from the monster (along x or along z); if
  14+ 3066              ; that way is blocked (a building, the base, the wall) it takes the other,
  15+ 3066              ; and if both are, it stands.  It only runs along roads.
  16+ 3066              ;
  17+ 3066              ; Base: landed on the landing pad (map code PAD_CODE), the passengers get off
  18+ 3066              ; one every DISEMBARK frames (a second) and are counted as saved.
  19+ 3066              ;
  20+ 3066              ; Rescue: when the craft has landed (speed 0, resting on the road or on the
  21+ 3066              ; roof under it), carries fewer than PASSENGER_MAX and a human stands within
  22+ 3066              ; RESCUE_R at the same height (a roof of the same height, or the road), the
  23+ 3066              ; human runs to it at HUMAN_RUN units a frame and climbs in.  A human on a
  24+ 3066              ; taller or lower roof cannot be reached.
  25+ 3066              ;
  26+ 3066              ; Each human is an HREC-byte record:
  27+ 3066              ;   +0,+1  x  (world units: high byte = cell, as for zombies)
  28+ 3066              ;   +2,+3  z
  29+ 3066              ;   +4,+5  y  height of its feet (roof height, or 0 on the road)
  30+ 3066              ;   +6     state (HS_*): 0 unused, 1 waiting in the city, 2 aboard the
  31+ 3066              ;          VTOL, 3 rescued (off at the landing pad), 4 dead
  32+ 3066              ;   +7,+8  cell (x, z) of its map dot
  33+ 3066              ;   +9     1 = map dot shown
  34+ 3066              ;   +10    hit points left (HUMAN_HP; a rocket blast, weapons.asm)
  35+ 3066              ;   +11,+12  cell (x, z) marked with CELL_HUMAN in city_map ($FF = none)
  36+ 3066              ;   +13    how it's drawn this frame: 0 standing, HUM_WAVING waving, or
  37+ 3066              ;          running (to the VTOL, or fleeing): its way + 1 (1 +z, 2 +x,
  38+ 3066              ;          3 -z, 4 -x, as a zombie's heading + 1)
  39+ 3066              ;   +14    fleeing: frames left (0: not fleeing)
  40+ 3066              ;   +15    fleeing: its way + 1 (as +13)
  41+ 3066              ;
  42+ 3066              ; Drawing: draw_cell (city page) tests the cell's CELL_HUMAN mark in
  43+ 3066              ; city_map (bit 6, set by hum_flags) and draws them with human_cell: after
  44+ 3066              ; the building on whose roof they stand, so the roof doesn't cover them.  With
  45+ 3066              ; OCCLUSION_CULL the cell goes on the draw list instead (as its city_col
  46+ 3066              ; address, $6000-$6FFF) and is drawn from there.
  47+ 3066              ;==============================================================================
  48+ 3066
  49+ 3066              HREC            equ 16
  50+ 3066              HUM_WAVING      equ 5               ; +13: waving (above the 4 ways)
  51+ 3066              HS_NONE         equ 0               ; human states (+6)
  52+ 3066              HS_WAIT         equ 1               ; waiting in the city to be rescued
  53+ 3066              HS_ABOARD       equ 2               ; aboard the VTOL
  54+ 3066              HS_SAVED        equ 3               ; rescued: off at the landing pad
  55+ 3066              HS_DEAD         equ 4               ; killed (a rocket blast, a ghost)
  56+ 3066

   1+ 38DD              ;==============================================================================
   2+ 38DD              ; Z-POLICE - interrupt mode 2 (in the zombie page, after map.asm: kept
   3+ 38DD              ; mapped in slot 1, so the table and routine are there whatever page is
   4+ 38DD              ; swapped in; the ROM replaces slot 1 only during esxDOS calls, when
   5+ 38DD              ; interrupts are off)
   6+ 38DD              ;
   7+ 38DD              ; In IM 2 an interrupt calls the address held in the word at I*256 + the
   8+ 38DD              ; byte on the data bus, which can be anything.  So:
   9+ 38DD              ;   * im2_table is 256 words, every one the address of im2_routine, at a
  10+ 38DD              ;     256-byte boundary (I holds the high byte of its address): any bus
  11+ 38DD              ;     byte, even $FF (bytes $FF and $100), reads a word inside it;
  12+ 38DD              ;   * an odd bus byte reads a word that straddles two entries, low byte
  13+ 38DD              ;     from one and high byte from the next, so im2_routine sits at an
  14+ 38DD              ;     address whose high and low bytes are the same (IM2_ROUTINE, $xyxy):
  15+ 38DD              ;     read either way round, it's the same address.
  16+ 38DD              ; im2_init sets I and IM 2 (start calls it after init_audio); start enables
  17+ 38DD              ; interrupts just before the main menu, and they stay on, 50 a second, except:
  18+ 38DD              ;   * over esxDOS calls (fh_rom_in / fh_rom_out): the ROM covers slot 1, this
  19+ 38DD              ;     page, so they are off and put back as they were;
  20+ 38DD              ;   * the span filler borrows SP (city.asm: PUSHes into Layer 2, slot 0).  An
  21+ 38DD              ;     interrupt there pushes its return address just below SP: into the
  22+ 38DD              ;     part of the span still to be filled, which the PUSHes then overwrite.
  23+ 38DD              ;     Interrupts are off from just before a span's last PUSH until SP is
  24+ 38DD              ;     back (push_blk), and a 1-pixel span doesn't borrow SP at all.
  25+ 38DD              ; The routine switches to its own stack at once, keeps every register, and
  26+ 38DD              ; touches only the AY ports (never $243B, the main code's NextReg port), and
  27+ 38DD              ; only while the engines are on (eng_on): code outside the interrupt writes
  28+ 38DD              ; the AY chips only with eng_on 0 (init_audio, engine_start).
  29+ 38DD              ;==============================================================================
  30+ 38DD
  31+ 38DD              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  32+ 38DD              ; Point I at the vector table and select interrupt mode 2.  (start enables
  33+ 38DD              ; interrupts later.)
  34+ 38DD              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  35+ 38DD              im2_init:
  36+ 38DD 3E 39                ld a,high im2_table
  37+ 38DF ED 47                ld i,a
  38+ 38E1 ED 5E                im 2
  39+ 38E3 C9                   ret
  40+ 38E4
  41+ 38E4 00 00 00...          ALIGN 256
  42+ 3900              im2_table:

  45+ 3B00                      ENDR
  46+ 3B00
  47+ 3B00              ; The routine's address: high byte = low byte, just past the table
  48+ 3B00              IM2_ROUTINE     equ ((high im2_table)+2)*$101
  49+ 3B00                      ASSERT $ <= IM2_ROUTINE
  50+ 3B00 00 00 00...          ds IM2_ROUTINE-$                ; (unused up to it)
  51+ 3B3B
  52+ 3B3B              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  53+ 3B3B              ; The interrupt routine, each video frame (50 a second): the engines' sound
  54+ 3B3B              ; (engine_tick) and the sound effects (sfx_tick).  On its own stack: SP may
  55+ 3B3B              ; be the span filler's.  It must never use the alternate registers (EXX,
  56+ 3B3B              ; EX AF,AF'): the city's cell walks keep their place in HL', DE' across
  57+ 3B3B              ; the whole drawing (draw_row, city.asm).
  58+ 3B3B              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  59+ 3B3B              im2_routine:
  60+ 3B3B ED 73 75 3C          ld (isr_sp),sp                  ; its own stack at once (no PUSH on
  61+ 3B3F 31 97 3C             ld sp,isr_stack                 ; a borrowed one)
  62+ 3B42 F5                   push af
  63+ 3B43 C5                   push bc
  64+ 3B44 D5                   push de
  65+ 3B45 E5                   push hl
  66+ 3B46 CD 57 3B             call engine_tick
  67+ 3B49 CD 09 3C             call sfx_tick
  68+ 3B4C E1                   pop hl
  69+ 3B4D D1                   pop de
  70+ 3B4E C1                   pop bc
  71+ 3B4F F1                   pop af
  72+ 3B50 ED 7B 75 3C          ld sp,(isr_sp)
  73+ 3B54 FB                   ei
  74+ 3B55 ED 4D                reti
  75+ 3B57                      ASSERT im2_routine == IM2_ROUTINE
  76+ 3B57                      ASSERT high im2_routine == low im2_routine
  77+ 3B57
  78+ 3B57              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  79+ 3B57              ; The VTOL's engines (audio.asm has the sound's constants and engine_start):
  80+ 3B57              ; jet turbines, on AY 1.  eng_cur is the speed the engines sound at, in
  81+ 3B57              ; 1/ENG_FRAC steps; each interrupt it follows the VTOL's, n = |speed| (at
  82+ 3B57              ; least 1: zero throttle idles as speed 1), by at most ENG_SPIN_UP going up
  83+ 3B57              ; and ENG_SPIN_DOWN going down: the turbines spool up, and down more slowly,
  84+ 3B57              ; instead of jumping.  From it:
  85+ 3B57              ;   A  noise, the roar: period ENG_NOISE0 - m*13/16, volume ENG_ROAR_VOL0 +
  86+ 3B57              ;      m*ENG_VOL_MUL/32
  87+ 3B57              ;      (m = eng_cur/ENG_FRAC, whole steps)
  88+ 3B57              ;   B  tone, the turbine whine: period ENG_WHINE0 - eng_cur*ENG_WHINE_STEP/
  89+ 3B57              ;      ENG_FRAC (sliding smoothly), volume ENG_WHINE_VOL0 + m*ENG_VOL_MUL/32
  90+ 3B57              ;   C  the same whine ENG_DETUNE periods lower and ENG_SHIMMER_VOL quieter:
  91+ 3B57              ;      the two beat, the turbines' shimmer
  92+ 3B57              ; Written only when eng_cur moves.  Nothing while eng_on is 0 (menus).
  93+ 3B57              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  94+ 3B57              engine_tick:
  95+ 3B57 3A 68 3C             ld a,(eng_on)
  96+ 3B5A B7                   or a
  97+ 3B5B C8                   ret z
  98+ 3B5C 3A 9F AF             ld a,(speed)
  99+ 3B5F B7                   or a
 100+ 3B60 F2 65 3B             jp p,.pos
 101+ 3B63 ED 44                neg                             ; reversing: its size
 102+ 3B65 B7           .pos:   or a
 103+ 3B66 20 01                jr nz,.n
 104+ 3B68 3C                   inc a                           ; zero throttle: idle, as speed 1
 105+ 3B69 FE 1D        .n:     cp SPEED_MAX+1
 106+ 3B6B 38 02                jr c,.nm
 107+ 3B6D 3E 1C                ld a,SPEED_MAX                  ; (boosting: as flat out)
 108+ 3B6F 5F           .nm:    ld e,a
 109+ 3B70 16 10                ld d,ENG_FRAC
 110+ 3B72 ED 30                mul d,e                         ; DE = the target, in 1/ENG_FRAC steps
 111+ 3B74 2A 73 3C             ld hl,(eng_cur)
 112+ 3B77 B7                   or a
 113+ 3B78 ED 52                sbc hl,de                       ; HL = eng_cur - target
 114+ 3B7A C8                   ret z                           ; there: nothing changes
 115+ 3B7B 38 09                jr c,.up
 116+ 3B7D 01 FE FF             ld bc,-ENG_SPIN_DOWN            ; above: down a step
 117+ 3B80 09                   add hl,bc
 118+ 3B81 30 0C                jr nc,.tgt                      ; (less than a step away: there)
 119+ 3B83 19                   add hl,de
 120+ 3B84 18 0A                jr .set
 121+ 3B86 01 04 00     .up:    ld bc,ENG_SPIN_UP               ; below: up a step
 122+ 3B89 09                   add hl,bc
 123+ 3B8A 38 03                jr c,.tgt                       ; (reached it)
 124+ 3B8C 19                   add hl,de
 125+ 3B8D 18 01                jr .set
 126+ 3B8F EB           .tgt:   ex de,hl
 127+ 3B90 22 73 3C     .set:   ld (eng_cur),hl
 128+ 3B93 3E FF                ld a,AY_SELECT|AY_LEFT|AY_RIGHT|AY_CHIP_1
 129+ 3B95 01 FD FF             ld bc,AY_CTRL_PORT
 130+ 3B98 ED 79                out (c),a
 131+ 3B9A E5                   push hl
 132+ 3B9B 54                   ld d,h                          ; B: the whine's period
 133+ 3B9C 5D                   ld e,l
 134+ 3B9D 29                   add hl,hl
 135+ 3B9E 19                   add hl,de                       ; eng_cur * ENG_WHINE_STEP
 136+ 3B9F EB                   ex de,hl
 137+ 3BA0 06 04                ld b,4
 138+ 3BA2 ED 2A                bsrl de,b                       ; / ENG_FRAC
 139+ 3BA4                      ASSERT ENG_WHINE_STEP == 3 && ENG_FRAC == 16
 140+ 3BA4 3E DE                ld a,ENG_WHINE0
 141+ 3BA6 93                   sub e
 142+ 3BA7 6F                   ld l,a                          ; L = the whine's period
 143+ 3BA8 5F                   ld e,a
 144+ 3BA9 3E 02                ld a,AY_TONE_B
 145+ 3BAB CD FF 3B             call isr_ay
 146+ 3BAE 3E 03                ld a,AY_TONE_B+1
 147+ 3BB0 1E 00                ld e,0
 148+ 3BB2 CD FF 3B             call isr_ay
 149+ 3BB5 7D                   ld a,l                          ; C: a little lower, to beat with B
 150+ 3BB6 C6 02                add a,ENG_DETUNE
 151+ 3BB8 5F                   ld e,a
 152+ 3BB9 3E 04                ld a,AY_TONE_C
 153+ 3BBB CD FF 3B             call isr_ay
 154+ 3BBE 3E 05                ld a,AY_TONE_C+1
 155+ 3BC0 1E 00                ld e,0
 156+ 3BC2 CD FF 3B             call isr_ay
 157+ 3BC5 D1                   pop de                          ; m = eng_cur / ENG_FRAC
 158+ 3BC6 06 04                ld b,4
 159+ 3BC8 ED 2A                bsrl de,b
 160+ 3BCA 63                   ld h,e                          ; H = m
 161+ 3BCB 54                   ld d,h                          ; A: the roar's noise period
 162+ 3BCC 1E 0D                ld e,ENG_NOISE_MUL
 163+ 3BCE ED 30                mul d,e
 164+ 3BD0 06 04                ld b,4
 165+ 3BD2 ED 2A                bsrl de,b                       ; m*13/16
 166+ 3BD4 3E 1D                ld a,ENG_NOISE0
 167+ 3BD6 93                   sub e
 168+ 3BD7 5F                   ld e,a
 169+ 3BD8 3E 06                ld a,AY_NOISE
 170+ 3BDA CD FF 3B             call isr_ay
 171+ 3BDD 54                   ld d,h                          ; the volumes: louder with speed
 172+ 3BDE 1E 07                ld e,ENG_VOL_MUL
 173+ 3BE0 ED 30                mul d,e
 174+ 3BE2 06 05                ld b,5
 175+ 3BE4 ED 2A                bsrl de,b
 176+ 3BE6 7B                   ld a,e
 177+ 3BE7 6F                   ld l,a                          ; L = m*ENG_VOL_MUL/32
 178+ 3BE8 C6 04                add a,ENG_ROAR_VOL0
 179+ 3BEA 5F                   ld e,a
 180+ 3BEB 3E 08                ld a,AY_VOL_A
 181+ 3BED CD FF 3B             call isr_ay
 182+ 3BF0 7D                   ld a,l
 183+ 3BF1 C6 02                add a,ENG_WHINE_VOL0
 184+ 3BF3 5F                   ld e,a
 185+ 3BF4 3E 09                ld a,AY_VOL_B
 186+ 3BF6 CD FF 3B             call isr_ay
 187+ 3BF9 7B                   ld a,e
 188+ 3BFA D6 02                sub ENG_SHIMMER_VOL
 189+ 3BFC 5F                   ld e,a
 190+ 3BFD 3E 0A                ld a,AY_VOL_C
 191+ 3BFF                      ; fall through
 192+ 3BFF
 193+ 3BFF              ; A = register, E = value: write it to the selected AY chip (here: the
 194+ 3BFF              ; interrupt's own, as ay_write is in a page that may not be in).  Keeps D,
 195+ 3BFF              ; E, HL.
 196+ 3BFF              isr_ay:
 197+ 3BFF 01 FD FF             ld bc,AY_CTRL_PORT
 198+ 3C02 ED 79                out (c),a
 199+ 3C04 06 BF                ld b,high AY_DATA_PORT
 200+ 3C06 ED 59                out (c),e
 201+ 3C08 C9                   ret
 202+ 3C09
 203+ 3C09              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 204+ 3C09              ; Sound effects, three voices: the weapons on AY 2 (sfx_req), explosions on
 205+ 3C09              ; AY 3's channels A and B (sfx2_req), and splats on AY 3's channel C
 206+ 3C09              ; (sfx3_req: a tone only, as the chip's noise is the explosions'), so none
 207+ 3C09              ; cuts another.  (The splats write only channel C's tone and volume, and
 208+ 3C09              ; the explosions leave channel C alone, its tone kept on in the mixer.)  The
 209+ 3C09              ; engines have AY 1.  The game asks for a sound by putting its number in a
 210+ 3C09              ; voice's request byte (SFX_*, audio.asm): one byte, so safe from any page
 211+ 3C09              ; at any time; only the interrupt writes the AY chips.  Each voice plays one
 212+ 3C09              ; sound at a time: a new one cuts the last.  A sound is a list of steps, one
 213+ 3C09              ; an interrupt (20 ms): each step is AY register / value pairs, ended by
 214+ 3C09              ; SFX_STEP (the next step next interrupt) or SFX_END (the sound is over).
 215+ 3C09              ; Nothing while eng_on is 0 (menus).
 216+ 3C09              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 217+ 3C09              sfx_tick:
 218+ 3C09 3A 68 3C             ld a,(eng_on)
 219+ 3C0C B7                   or a
 220+ 3C0D C8                   ret z
 221+ 3C0E 21 69 3C             ld hl,sfx_req                   ; the weapons, AY 2
 222+ 3C11 3E FE                ld a,AY_SELECT|AY_LEFT|AY_RIGHT|AY_CHIP_2
 223+ 3C13 CD 23 3C             call sfx_voice
 224+ 3C16 21 6C 3C             ld hl,sfx2_req                  ; explosions, AY 3 (A, B)
 225+ 3C19 3E FD                ld a,AY_SELECT|AY_LEFT|AY_RIGHT|AY_CHIP_3
 226+ 3C1B CD 23 3C             call sfx_voice
 227+ 3C1E 21 6F 3C             ld hl,sfx3_req                  ; splats, AY 3 (C)
 228+ 3C21 3E FD                ld a,AY_SELECT|AY_LEFT|AY_RIGHT|AY_CHIP_3
 229+ 3C23                      ; fall through
 230+ 3C23
 231+ 3C23              ; HL -> a voice (its request byte, then its sound's next step, a word: 0
 232+ 3C23              ; none), A = its AY chip's select value: start a sound asked for, and play
 233+ 3C23              ; the next step
 234+ 3C23              sfx_voice:
 235+ 3C23 32 72 3C             ld (sv_sel),a
 236+ 3C26 7E                   ld a,(hl)                       ; a new sound asked for?
 237+ 3C27 B7                   or a

 239+ 3C2A 36 00                ld (hl),0                       ; (taken)

2112  0200                      MMU SPRBANK_SLOT e, PAGE_SPR0, SPRBANK_ADDR

# file opened: sprite_data.asm
   1+ E000              ;==============================================================================
   2+ E000              ; Z-POLICE - sprite pattern banks (8K pages, assembled at $E000)
   3+ E000              ;
   4+ E000              ; Hardware sprite patterns are only needed when they are loaded into the
   5+ E000              ; sprite pattern memory, so they live in their own pages, out of the way,
   6+ E000              ; each with its own loader so that no resident memory is used:
   7+ E000              ;
   8+ E000              ;       nextreg CODE_MMU,PAGE_SPR0      ; the bank into slot 7
   9+ E000              ;       call spr_load_bank              ; copy its patterns
  10+ E000              ;
  11+ E000              ; Call it from outside slot 7 (resident code or a game logic page in slot
  12+ E000              ; 6), and page back whatever slot 7 had afterwards if it is still needed.
  13+ E000              ; spr_load_bank is the same address ($E000) in every bank.
  14+ E000              ;
  15+ E000              ; Each bank (SPRBANK_ADDR = $E000):
  16+ E000              ;   +0          spr_load_bank: the loader (SPRB_LOADER), the same in each
  17+ E000              ;   SPRB_COUNT  number of patterns (1..31: 256 bytes each, 8-bit 16x16)
  18+ E000              ;   SPRB_FIRST  the pattern number the first one loads to (0..63)
  19+ E000              ;   SPRB_DATA   the patterns, one after another
  20+ E000              ; More sprites: add a bank (the next free page, its own PAGE_SPRn in
  21+ E000              ; memory_bank_defs.asm, the MMU / ORG lines in zpolice.asm and a block here
  22+ E000              ; starting with SPRB_LOADER).
  23+ E000              ;==============================================================================
  24+ E000
  25+ E000              ; Copy this bank's patterns into the sprite pattern memory.  Runs from the
  26+ E000              ; bank itself: reads only, so it needs no variables.
  27+ E000                      MACRO SPRB_LOADER
  28+ E000 ~                    ld a,(SPRBANK_ADDR+SPRB_FIRST)  ; from this pattern
  29+ E000 ~                    ld bc,SPR_SLOT_PORT
  30+ E000 ~                    out (c),a
  31+ E000 ~                    ld a,(SPRBANK_ADDR+SPRB_COUNT)
  32+ E000 ~                    ld d,a
  33+ E000 ~                    ld hl,SPRBANK_ADDR+SPRB_DATA
  34+ E000 ~                    ld c,SPR_PAT_PORT
  35+ E000 ~            .lp:    ld b,0                          ; 256 bytes a pattern
  36+ E000 ~                    otir
  37+ E000 ~                    dec d
  38+ E000 ~                    jr nz,.lp
  39+ E000 ~                    ret
  40+ E000                      ENDM
  41+ E000
  42+ E000              spr_load_bank   equ SPRBANK_ADDR        ; the loader, in every bank
  43+ E000              SPRB_COUNT      equ spr_bank0_hdr-spr_bank0
  44+ E000              SPRB_FIRST      equ SPRB_COUNT+1
  45+ E000              SPRB_DATA       equ SPRB_COUNT+2
  46+ E000
  47+ E000              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  48+ E000              ; Bank 0 (PAGE_SPR0): the human status sprites (patterns 0-3), then the
  49+ E000              ; compass bar's letters, dots and pointer (CSPR_*, hud_sprites.asm)
  50+ E000              ; (zpolice.asm maps PAGE_SPR0 to SPRBANK_SLOT, ORG SPRBANK_ADDR, first)
